introduction.text: The Centrale Montemartini is a former power plant in Rome that now functions as a museum, notable for its blend of industrial machinery and classical antiquities.

history.description: Inaugurated on 30 June 1912 as Rome's first municipal power plant.
Inaugurated two 7500 HP diesel engines on 21 April 1933.
Survived Allied bombing during World War II; remained the sole power plant for Rome.
Opened as the second pole of the Capitoline Museums in 1997.
Expanded in November 2016 with the former boiler room 2, housing the pontifical train carriages of Pope Pius IX.
Opened a room dedicated to imperial sarcophagi in December 2017.

design.description: The building's industrial architecture was restored by Acea and the Capitoline Superintendency, preserving original machinery and integrating museum spaces.
Two large iron lamp posts designed by Duilio Cambellotti adorn the exterior.
Restoration work in the 1990s converted the machine rooms into exhibition halls while retaining the original industrial layout.

art.description: Displays Roman Republican sculptures, sarcophagi from the 2nd to 4th centuries CE, and other antiquities.
Industrial machinery, including steam turbines and diesel engines, serves as a backdrop for the classical artworks.
